rules: Killing the Black Dragon wins the match for the side of the player who dealt it the most damage.
At most 2 of each second class per side: checked when the teams form, and again at the Lv40 class trial and at Rebirth.

Second classes: Champion from Carsise Swordsman; Cleric from Ami Herbalist or Lance Herbalist or Phyllis Herbalist; Crusader from Lance Swordsman or Phyllis Swordsman; Seal Master from Ami Herbalist or Lance Herbalist or Phyllis Herbalist; Sharpshooter from Lance Hunter or Phyllis Hunter; Voyager from Ami Explorer or Lance Explorer or Phyllis Explorer.
Gear grows with you: as you level, the pieces you wear and the ones in your bag (not the bank or a vault) step up to the next tier on their own.
Chaos gear levels with its wearer.
Boss drop tables pay out on the first kill of each boss in a match; later kills still grant gold and the boss's other rewards.
Every kill shares its gold, an Auto Ration and a chance at a fairy stat fruit with each teammate who receives the gold.
Up to 3 sockets on a piece of gear.
Physical and magic resistance cap at 70; gear gives magic resistance equal to its physical resistance.
Skill bars are saved per account and per class, automatically.

Kylin.summary: Turns some of the damage you take into healing.
Kylin.detail: One hit in ten heals you instead of hurting you. Wearing any class ring strengthens it further — closer to one hit in five, and the healing is larger. It works on its own once the three pieces are on; there is nothing to activate.

BlackDragon.summary: Spreads healing across the team, and adds a strike for some classes.
BlackDragon.detail: When a healer casts Heal, there is a one-in-five chance it echoes to every ally in the match for half its value. Wearing any class ring also unlocks Draconic Retribution, which differs by class. The heal echo needs a healer in the party to matter.

Chaos.summary: Every kill makes you hit harder, up to +30%.
Chaos.detail: With the full set and any class ring, each kill or assist adds +2% attack, up to +30% at fifteen. The count carries through your own death and resets when the match ends. It only exists inside a running match, so this panel cannot show it on your numbers.

Death.summary: The only set that changes your actual stats — and each class gets its own.
Death.detail: Six sets share the name, one per advanced class. Each raises a few of your stats by a percentage of what your gear already gives, and adds an effect of its own. The percentages stack on top of your gear rather than multiplying with each other. Your class's row is highlighted below.
